## Fundamental Definitions Associated with LOD

In the current context, there are six different levels of development that are defined by the **[American Institute of Architects (AIA)](https://www.aia.org/ "American Institute of Architects (AIA)").** According to AIA, LOD outlines the design requirements at each stage.

At LOD 100, which is the pre-design stage, the model consists of 2D symbols and the masses to signify an element’s existence.

At LOD 200, the elements are partially defined by outlining their approximate quantity, size, shape, and location.

By LOD 300, the elements are defined with **[exact BIM dimensions](https://www.united-bim.com/what-are-bim-dimensions-3d-4d-5d-6d-7d-bim-explained-definition-benefits/ "BIM Dimensions – 3D, 4D, 5D, 6D, and 7D BIM Explaination")** and their relative positions bolstering precision.

LOD 350 describes the information about an element precisely and outlines an element’s relation and connection with other components.

The **[LOD 400](https://www.united-bim.com/lod-400-bim-services/ "LOD 400 Services")** level outlines the basic information about the construction of various elements.

By [LOD 500](https://www.united-bim.com/lod-500-bim-modeling-services-facility-management/ "LOD 500"), the model begins representing the real-life functions of elements in a real building, which is exactly where its value extends into operations and maintenance, and [why facility teams start depending heavily on it](https://www.united-bim.com/blog-why-facility-managers-demand-lod-500/). Here are all the levels of development with their definitions in detail.

### 01.

### LOD 100 - Conceptual

The Model Element may be graphically represented in the Model with a symbol or other generic representation. Information related to the Model Element can be derived from other Model Elements. Any information derived from LOD 100 elements must be considered approximate.

### 02.

### LOD 200 - Approximate Geometry

The Model Element is graphically represented within the Model as a generic system, object, or assembly with approximate quantities, size, shape, location, and orientation. Any information derived from LOD 200 elements must be considered approximate.

### 03.

### LOD 300 - Precise Geometry

The Model Element is graphically represented within the Model as a specific system, object or assembly in terms of quantity, size, shape, location, and orientation. Non-graphic information may also be attached to the Model Element. The project origin is defined and the element is located accurately with respect to the project origin.

### 04.

### LOD 350 - Precise Geometry with Connections

LOD 350 The Model Element is graphically represented within the Model as a specific system, object, or assembly in terms of quantity, size, shape, location, orientation, and interfaces with other building systems. Non-graphic information may also be attached to the Model Element.

### 05.

### LOD 400- Fabrication-ready Geometry

LOD 400 The Model Element is graphically represented within the Model as a specific system, object or assembly in terms of size, shape, location, quantity, and orientation with detailing, fabrication, assembly, and installation information. Non-graphic information may also be attached to the Model Element.

### 06.

### LOD 500 - Operational/As-built Models

LOD 500 The Model Element is a field verified representation in terms of size, shape, location, quantity, and orientation. Non-graphic information may also be attached to the Model Elements. LOD 500 represents field-verified, as-built conditions and is commonly used for operations, asset tracking, and long-term facility management.

With the help of LOD specifications, communication and collaboration can become easier and faster, making room for the efficient deployment of resources at all levels of design and construction. In an era where everything is handled digitally and all critical projects make use of a 3D model, it becomes hard for designers to make other teams understand the project expectations. Most often, handling a BIM model comes with a unique challenge- different people perceive different definitions of completion.

LOD creates a standardized definition of what completion means and eliminates the chances of discrepancies associated with project completion. Using LOD, teams working under different disciplines can communicate with each other in a better way with greater clarity. 5 Steps to Master LOD 350 for Successful BIM Delivery
LOD 350 is not just another milestone. It’s the critical bridge between design and real-world construction. Get it right, and your projects flow seamlessly. Get it wrong, and you face clashes, delays, and rework on site.
Here are 5 essential steps to master LOD 350 :
🔹 Step 1: Model Real-World Connections
Don't just model objects model how they interact. Beams to bolts, ducts to hangers, walls to openings. Focus on constructability, not just appearance.
🔹 Step 2: Coordinate Early and Deeply
Use BIM coordination to proactively resolve issues between architecture, structure, and MEP, not reactively during construction.
🔹 Step 3: Enrich Your Models with information
LOD 350 is not just geometry. Add key information: system names, material types, component IDs, installation requirements, and metadata needed for handover.
🔹 Step 4: Model for Construction Reality, Not Just for Design Intent
Think like the site team: clearances, tolerances, and maintenance access. Make sure your model is actually buildable.
🔹 Step 5: Define Standards, Roles, and Expectations from Day One
Set crystal-clear modeling guidelines, ownership matrices, and review protocols in your BEP and project kickoff.

Understanding the Levels of Development (LOD) in BIM 🏗️
Building Information Modeling (BIM) isn’t just about creating 3D models — it’s about accurately representing the design, construction, and lifecycle of a building.
This image perfectly illustrates the progressive Levels of Development (LOD) in BIM:
🔹 LOD 100 – Conceptual design: basic massing and overall form.
🔹 LOD 200 – Approximate geometry: elements defined with approximate size, shape, and location.
🔹 LOD 300 – Detailed design: accurate geometry and spatial coordination.
🔹 LOD 400 – Fabrication: model includes fabrication, assembly, and detailed information.
🔹 LOD 500 – As-built: final model representing the completed construction with verified field data.
Each level enhances project collaboration, reduces risk, and improves decision-making — from concept to construction to operation.
